reading.body:
Humane Intelligence is recorded as a 2022 Texas nonprofit with no AI products, no litigation, and no MCP servers, but 126 Texas law exposure entries.

The only substantial data point is the law exposure count. Everything else in the record is an absence: no products, no cases, no MCP servers, no aliases. A nonprofit founded in 2022 and headquartered in Katy, Texas, with a website that returned only a placeholder message at collection time, leaves almost nothing to characterize what the organization actually does.

The 126 Texas law exposure entries are the one figure that carries weight, and the data does not explain what they represent. They could be filings, citations, or registry entries. Without that definition, the count cannot be read as risk, activity, or scale. It is a number attached to a Texas code reference and nothing more.

For AI specifically, this record supports no claim about compute, data centers, or power. There is no product, no infrastructure, and no disclosed operation to connect to the grid. The honest reading is that the data is thin, and the absences should be treated as gaps in collection rather than as facts about the organization.

profile_text.body:
Humane Intelligence is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2022 and headquartered in Katy, Texas. It describes itself as dedicated to breaking down barriers to AI deployment for social good, and says it collaboratively designs and runs rigorous evaluations that make AI systems more accountable, responsible, and fair.

The organization describes three main offerings. AI red teaming is a semi-structured testing approach to assess and improve the safety and effectiveness of AI models and systems by identifying vulnerabilities and limitations; Humane Intelligence offers red teaming events as a paid service using its own software, which it says it released under an open source license in September 2026. AI contextual evaluations are described as rigorous, mixed-method, bespoke evaluations of a model or system's performance for a specified problem space, with ontology-based contextual AI evaluations developed in 2026 and run as a paid service. Bias bounties are collaboratively designed sets of challenges bringing together researchers, impacted communities, and domain experts to examine and improve AI and ML systems, models, and datasets; the final self-hosted bias bounty closed in November 2025, and the first bias bounty on Zindi, described as a global data science challenge platform, launched in August 2026. The company's web application was built for data collection at hosted red teaming events and for contextual evaluation services, was released as open source in September 2026, and a new client-facing version is stated as available in October 2026.

The record shows no tracked products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers. It lists the organization as a nonprofit, and its law exposure is recorded for Texas with a count of 126.
